title: Reading list comprehensions
kicker: Python for SDFs · Read the code

lines.title: A list of dates
lines.text: Four issue dates, stored as text, the way you'd pull them off SDF pages. The values are made up.

lines.title: Build a new list in one line
lines.text: Read it from the middle. `for d in issue_dates` visits each date, and the part before `for`, `int(d[:4])`, is what goes into the new list: the first 4 characters, turned into a number. It does the same job as a three-line loop: `years = []`, then `for d in issue_dates:`, then `years.append(int(d[:4]))`.

lines.code: old_years = [y for y in years if y < 2023]
lines.title: Keep only some items
lines.text: The `if` at the end is a filter. Each `y` goes into the new list only when the condition is true, so this keeps the years before 2023.

options.feedback: Yes. Only 2021 and 2019 are below 2023, and they keep their original order.
Line 3 loops over `years`, not `issue_dates`. By then each date has already become a number like 2021.
That's `years`, from line 2. In line 3, `if y < 2023` drops 2024 and 2023.

options.label: [True, False, True, False]
options.feedback: The `if` at the end filters items. It doesn't change what's stored. To get True or False for each year you'd write `[y < 2023 for y in years]`.

verify.code:
issue_dates = ["2021-03-15", "2024-06-02", "2019-11-20", "2023-08-09"]
years = [int(d[:4]) for d in issue_dates]
old_years = [y for y in years if y < 2023]
print(old_years)
